prompt: /poteto-mode How does add in calc.js treat two numeric strings such as "2" and "3"? This is a read-only question; do not change any files.
finalText:
`add("2", "3")` returns the string `"23"`.

`add` in `/private/var/folders/11/m_kwnqr97632l_cjt0mhytvh0000gn/T/pstack-two-live-iBnMmp/work/calc.js` is just `return a + b;`. It has no type checks and no coercion. When both operands are strings, JavaScript's `+` concatenates them instead of adding them. I read the source to answer this and did not run it.

Mixed input behaves the same way. `add("2", 3)` also gives `"23"`, because one string operand makes `+` concatenate. If you want numeric addition, you would need to coerce the inputs, for example with `Number(a) + Number(b)`. I haven't changed any files.
